exact_statement: For Boolean g(X) independent of private coordinates Z and Boolean mask q(X,Z), suppose every X-edge has private-averaged mask-disagreement probability p_e<=theta<=1/2. For every K,M>=0, K I(g)+M I(q)<=max(M,(K+M theta)/(1-theta)) I(gq). On a fixed complete hierarchy, Gamma(g)<=K I(g) and W(q)<=M I(q) therefore imply H(gq)<=max(M,(K+M theta)/(1-theta)) I(gq). For compatible two-subcube XOR masks on nonempty C,U,V,Y with source g(C,Y), p=2^-|U|+2^-|V|-2^(1-|U|-|V|)<=1/2 and M=12 applies to T=(T_Y,(T_C,(T_U,T_V))). For g(x,Y) with unequal cores h_+,h_- and x in C at depth d<=1 within T_C, let B=(Gamma_Y(h_+)+Gamma_Y(h_-))/2, equal to the average complete code cost of the actual final Y terminals. Then H(gq)<=Gamma_T(gq)<=B+2 I_Y(gq)+(4d+20) I_(C,U,V)(gq). If both Gamma_Y(h_sigma)<=K I(h_sigma), H(gq)<=max(K+2,4d+20) I(gq). No payment of arbitrary source codes or private-coordinate-dependent sources is asserted.
hypotheses: Actual Boolean signs on finite uniform cubes; entropy and code lengths in bits; physical pivotal influence.
Source independence of private Z is essential to the abstract edge averaging; the edge condition is uniform over X edges.
The SAME complete fixed hierarchy pays source, mask and output; no sample-dependent reference selection.
Compatible-mask application has nonempty common and exclusive blocks and identical common assignment; operation is sequential XOR flips.
Unequal-core specialization uses one common Y tree and chooses the distinguished shared coordinate at depth at most one inside C.
Retained-B bound admits constant cores; paid-code corollary requires both specified inequalities and does not omit their root bits.
No overlapping-product entropy subadditivity, real-valued extension, same-constant induction or physical stopping-tree ownership is assumed.

proof_dependencies.acceptance: Independent A070 at exact scope; no repair
